implementation: A domain-separated lowercase SHA-256 task reference now binds the fixed Task Spec digest, durable TaskCreated admission command (therefore client_request_id), run_id, and ingress profile digest. Submit projects that reference; a new Status process replays the verified TaskCreated command and deterministically recomputes the same reference. No public schema, Task Spec, PostgreSQL schema, One Writer, lease, fencing, config, script, or cleanup change.

It is distinct from earlier LATTICE_TASK_SUBMIT_STATUS_ONLY, LATTICE_TASK_INGRESS_PROFILE_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH, and TTL/listener preflight failures. pros: minimal two-file reversible change; preserves one fixed Task Spec and all writer/lease/fence bindings; no persistence/schema migration; deterministic across fresh Status via already durable replay; different client_request_id cannot reproduce the old fixed spec-digest reference
cons: Status must replay TaskCreated before comparing a syntactically valid task_ref; pre-remediation old task_ref values are not aliases for the new derived reference; live interoperability is intentionally unverified here
alternative: Make the complete Task Spec/binding itself vary by client_request_id/run/profile, or persist a new first-class task_ref field. Both would touch Task Domain/Ledger/Writer Lease/status contracts or PostgreSQL schema and expand the security-sensitive ownership surface.
why_current: It is the lightest and fastest reversible fix because it separates the opaque public handle from the authoritative fixed spec digest, uses facts already durable and independently replay-verified, and changes no public JSON shape or governance owner.
